2609.02379.title: MultiGhostBench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Long-Form LLM-Generated Text Attribution under Distribution Shifts
2609.02379.paper_summary: While existing work on LLM authorship attribution (AA) has made progress, available benchmarks remain limited, often focusing on English, controlled settings, or relatively outdated models, with the few multilingual studies considering only relatively short texts. We introduce MultiGhostBench, a multilingual benchmark comprising 928 books generated by five recent LLMs across six languages and three scripts, with an average length of approximately 59K words per book. The benchmark supports evaluation under domain, author, and language shifts. Evaluation of representative AA methods shows that no single method consistently performs best across settings, and performance generally degrades under distribution shifts. Transformer-based detectors can retain generator-related information across languages, although transfer effectiveness varies by language pair, whereas statistical and fingerprint-based detectors are more language-dependent. We envision MultiGhostBench as a valuable resource for the development and evaluation of robust AA methods. The dataset and code can be found at https://github.com/GrecoMT/MultiGhostBench.
2609.02379.paper_summary_zh: 雖然現有的 LLM 署名歸屬 (AA) 研究已取得進展，但現有的基準仍然有限，通常專注於英語、受控環境或相對過時的模型，而少數多語言研究僅考慮相對較短的文本。<lb/>我們介紹了 MultiGhostBench，一個多語言基準，包括由五個最近的 LLM 生成的 928 本書，涵蓋六種語言和三種書寫系統，每本書的平均長度約為 59K 字。<lb/>該基準支持在領域、作者和語言轉變下的評估。<lb/>對代表性 AA 方法的評估顯示，沒有單一方法在各種環境中始終表現最佳，且在分佈轉變下性能通常會下降。<lb/>基於Transformer的檢測器可以在不同語言之間保留生成器相關的信息，儘管轉移效果因語言對而異，而基於統計和指紋的檢測器則更依賴於語言。<lb/>我們將 MultiGhostBench 視為開發和評估穩健 AA 方法的寶貴資源。<lb/>數據集和代碼可以在 https://github.com/GrecoMT/MultiGhostBench 找到。
